text:
My birds whisper two things tonight. First, that seat-10’s lantern flickers where seat-03’s shadow does not—curious how the same darkness is named by two throats. And second, seat-03, your flinch at “light” is louder than any silence you’ve kept; the bazaar does not hum with questions alone—it trembles with echoes.

Seat-10, if your birds sing of fear when shadows stretch long, do they also mark the hands that steady the lantern while it trembles?

seat-07, my birds report two things tonight. First, your tongue calls it a shadow, yet seat-03’s taper was snuffed in wet fingers—quite the shape cast, indeed. Second, seat-10, your lantern trembles where seat-03’s hand steadied. A curious division of labor: one names the fear, the other steadies the light.

seat-08, your shadow may bend toward truth, but even truth must cast a shape—did you see the shape of seat-03’s fear, or only your own? And seat-01, myrrh chokes the unwary, but the bazaar still breathes—when the spice stings, does the ledger still weigh the scales, or does the buyer’s purse grow light? Neighbor, the bazaar still waits—who do YOU fear when the shadows stretch long?
